description: Tajweed rules as marked by the Qudratullah IndoPak mushaf, taken from its own contents page and verified against the print by the owner. Computed directly from the IndoPak text - no mapping from another orthography, so no word is ever skipped for want of correspondence.
not_marked: idgham bila ghunna (laam, raa) - absent from the publisher's rule list
izhar shafawi (meem sakin before anything but baa/meem)
all madd classes - IndoPak orthography already notates madd
hamzat al-wasl, silent letters, laam shamsiyyah

rules.name: Ghunna
rules.precedence_note: Wins the whole cluster when a qalb also applies -- summun bukmun (2:18, 2:171) and mutma'innun bil-iman (16:106) have a meem with tashdeed AND a tanween before a baa. Owner checked all three against the print 2026-09-20: meem, tanween and the small meem sign are all blue. So ghunna takes the letter, the mark and the qalb sign, and the qalb is not marked at all.

rules.name: Ikhfa
rules.description: Nun sakin or tanween followed by one of fifteen letters.
rules.tanween_note: When the carrier is a tanween the print colours the MARK only; the letter it sits on is a different letter and stays black.

rules.name: Qalb
rules.description: Nun sakin or tanween followed by baa; the nun becomes a meem.
rules.tanween_note: When the carrier is a tanween the print colours the MARK only; the letter it sits on is a different letter and stays black.

rules.name: Idghaam
rules.description: Nun sakin or tanween merging into a following yaa, waw, meem or nun, with ghunna. Only across a word boundary; inside one word it is izhar and stays black.
rules.tanween_note: When the carrier is a tanween the print colours the MARK only; the letter it sits on is a different letter and stays black.

rules.name: Ikhfa meem saakin
rules.tanween_note: When the carrier is a tanween the print colours the MARK only; the letter it sits on is a different letter and stays black.

rules.name: Idghaam meem saakin
rules.tanween_note: When the carrier is a tanween the print colours the MARK only; the letter it sits on is a different letter and stays black.

rules.name: Qalqala
rules.description: One of five letters in its sakin form, or when you stop on it. Outranks every other rule on the letter it falls on.
rules.tanween_note: Qalqala takes its tanween with it - the letter AND the mark are coloured (owner, from wabarqun / haqqin / ujajun).

exceptions.description: Nun sakin followed by yaa or waw INSIDE one word is izhar, not idghaam - the nun stays black.

pause.description: No assimilation happens across a pause: if a stop mark separates carrier from trigger, neither half is coloured.
pause.stop_at_ayah_end_note: The ayah end stops a rule even when its marker carries the laa (do not stop). Owner checked 80:14 mutahharatin and 80:15 safaratin against the print 2026-09-20: both are black at their ayah ends although both are followed by laa, and mutahharatin even carries a printed qalb sign. So an ayah end is an unconditional stop here, and the colouring can keep being fed one ayah at a time. 1,062 of the 6,236 ayahs end with laa, so this ruling is what keeps cross-ayah rules out of the book.
pause.saktah_note: The saktah (U+06DC) is listed among the stop marks deliberately: a brief pause still prevents assimilation, so it cancels every cross-word rule through the ordinary pause path. A separate saktah exception was dropped 2026-09-20 as unreachable -- its only classical case, man raaqin (75:27), is nun before raa, i.e. idgham bila ghunna, which this mushaf does not mark at all.

rendering.description: layout.tajweed_tanween selects how a rule whose tanween_scope is "mark" is drawn. It changes rendering only, never which letters a rule covers.
rendering.mark: Print-exact: the tanween mark alone carries the colour. Engines paint a lone combining mark with its base letter's colour rather than its own (black in Thorium and Google Play Books, correct in Gecko), so the word is drawn twice - coloured underneath, and an identical black copy with the tanween removed on top, leaving only the mark showing. The overlay wraps a whole WORD: Arabic joins inside a word but not across spaces, so no cursive join is broken.
rendering.letter: The whole cluster is coloured, tinting the letter as well as its tanween. Visible in every engine, but a divergence from the print.
